title: Decimals: 38 digits, the larger scale, half to even
verdict: `Decimal(38, max(s₁, s₂))`; rounds half to even; raises on overflow and on `/ 0`
description: Arithmetic on decimals returns `Decimal(38, max(s₁, s₂))` for `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` (an integer operand counts as scale 0), and `sum` returns `Decimal(38, s)`: the result's precision is always 38, so `Decimal(6, 2) * 1000` gives 9999990.00 and overflows only past 38 digits, where it raises (`ComputeError`).

A result with more digits than the scale rounds half to even: `0.05 * 0.5` is 0.02, `1.00 / 8` is 0.12, a cast from scale 3 to scale 1 makes 1.050 into 1.0 and 1.150 into 1.2, and a double cast to a decimal rounds half to even on its exact value (0.625 is 0.62). Division by zero raises. `mean` of decimals is a `Float64`.
The docs are silent on the result's precision and scale and on the half-to-even rounding: a docs gap.
reference: `functions_arithmetic_decimal.yaml` gives the result types (multiply: scale s₁ + s₂, divide: max(6, s₁ + p₂ + 1), precision capped at 38 by borrowing scale) and no rounding; the reference rounds half away from zero (`decimal_rescale`). Decimal division is refused until #27. ST-8 records the open rounding.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: streaming decimal sum: i128 checked_add with a sticky overflow sentinel; finish() raises 'overflow in decimal addition in sum' past 38 digits.
`test_decimal_arithmetic`: Decimal(20, 10) + - * / all give Decimal(38, 10); 0.1 / 20.1 == 0.0049751244, 10.1 * 10.19 == 102.919; eager, in memory.
`test_decimal_arithmetic_schema_int`: an integer operand counts as scale 0, result Decimal(38, 6); s / 3 == 0.333333.
sum to Decimal(38, s), overflow past 38 digits raises ComputeError, partial sums past 38 digits allowed; parametrized engine in ['streaming', 'in-memory'].
Precision 38 is the default and the maximum (SRC py-polars/src/polars/datatypes/classes.py L447-L459); silent on result precision and scale of arithmetic and on its rounding.
